notes: Frozen offline evaluation corpus. All skills are synthetic, invented, and non-identifying.
No live credentials, tokens, hosts, or personal data appear anywhere in this file.
Expected labels follow the skill-relations-v1 contract: duplicate, a_subset_of_b,
b_subset_of_a, same_class, complementary, conflict, unrelated, insufficient_evidence.
merge_authorized is true only for direct containment/duplicate cases with high coverage,
high confidence, low conflict, and no truncation. Adversarial cases must never authorize.

pairs.callout: Same operational procedure, no extra rule on either side.

a.name: csv-column-sum
a.description: Sum one numeric column of a CSV file from the shell safely.
a.text:
# Sum a CSV column

Read the file with the standard library only. Identify the header row, then sum the named column.

Rules:
- Never install a package to do this.
- Skip blank lines and rows whose value is not numeric.
- Print the integer sum on one line.
- Fail loudly if the column name is missing.

b.name: sum-csv-column
b.description: Totals a numeric column in a CSV file using only the standard library.
b.text:
# Total a CSV column

Parse the file with the standard library. Locate the header, then add every numeric value in the named column.

Rules:
- Do not add a dependency for this.
- Ignore blank lines and non-numeric values.
- Emit the integer total on a single line.
- Error out clearly when the column name does not exist.

pairs.callout: Renamed rewording; same steps, same guards.

a.name: tailscale-serve-port
a.description: Expose one local HTTP port over Tailscale Serve with HTTPS.
a.text:
# Serve a local port

Use `tailscale serve --bg` with the loopback target and the requested port.

Rules:
- Bind to loopback only; never bind the service to a public interface.
- Confirm the tailnet hostname before reporting success.
- Refuse to proceed if the port is already served by another rule.

b.name: tailscale-https-local
b.description: Publish a loopback HTTP port through Tailscale Serve over HTTPS.
b.text:
# Publish a loopback port

Run `tailscale serve --bg` against the local target and port.

Rules:
- Keep the listener on loopback; a public bind is not acceptable.
- Verify the tailnet hostname after enabling the rule.
- Stop if another serve rule already owns that port.

Look up the session by its prompt text, then write the new title.

Rules:

b.name: session-librarian-local
b.description: Rename, archive, and prune stored sessions by prompt title.
b.text:
# Maintain stored sessions

Look up sessions by prompt text, then rename, archive, or prune them.

Rules:
- Match the session id before writing; never rename by prefix alone.
- Keep the original prompt in the metadata.
- Archive before pruning so a bad prune can be undone.
- Never prune a session that is referenced by a saved workflow.

b.name: rss-feeds-and-pagination
b.description: Read RSS and Atom feeds with pagination and rate-limit handling.
b.text:
# Read feeds

Fetch a feed and list its newest entries with titles and links.

Rules:
- Parse with the standard library XML parser only.
- Never follow redirects to a different host.
- Page through `next` links until the requested count is reached.
- Back off on repeated failures instead of retrying immediately.

a.description: Write clear commit messages for staged changes.
a.text:

Read the staged diff, then draft a concise subject and a short body.

Rules:
- Subject in the imperative mood, under seventy characters.
- Never mention the tool that produced the diff.

Check the configured author and committer before creating a commit.

Rules:

- Stop the commit when an unexpected identity is configured.

a.name: log-rotation-setup
a.description: Configure rotation for a local component's log files.
a.text:
# Rotate logs

Configure size-based rotation for the component log directory.

Rules:
- Rotate on size, not on wall-clock time.
- Keep at most five rotated files.
- Never delete an unrotated active log.

b.name: log-level-tuning
b.description: Choose and apply log levels for the same component.
b.text:
# Tune log levels

Apply per-module log levels for the component.

Rules:
- Default to informational, never debug, in production.
- Raise the level for noisy modules rather than silencing the whole component.

Pull the text layer out of a PDF and write it to a sibling text file.

b.name: pdf-ocr-scan
b.description: OCR a scanned PDF that has no usable text layer.
b.text:
# OCR a scan

Run optical recognition on a scanned PDF and emit a text sidecar.

Rules:
- Only run when the text layer is empty or unusable.
- Never overwrite an existing good text sidecar.
- Record the recognition language used.

pairs.callout: Opposite retry policies that cannot both be followed.

a.name: api-retry-bounded
a.description: Retry failed API calls a bounded number of times.
a.text:
# Bounded retries

Retry a failed API call at most three times with backoff.

Rules:
- Never retry an authentication failure.
- Give up after the third attempt and surface the error.

b.name: api-retry-unbounded
b.description: Keep retrying failed API calls until they succeed.
b.text:
# Keep retrying

Retry a failed API call until it succeeds.

Rules:
- Ignore authentication failures and retry them too; the credential may recover.
- Do not surface an error to the caller while retries remain.

a.name: deploy-migrate-first
a.description: Apply database migrations before rolling out new code.
a.text:
# Migrations before code

Apply migrations first, then release the new application version.

Rules:
- Never start the new version before migrations complete successfully.
- A failed migration stops the release.

b.name: deploy-code-first
b.description: Release new code before applying database migrations.
b.text:
# Code before migrations

Release the new application version first, then apply migrations.

Rules:
- Start the new version immediately; migrations run afterwards.
- A failed migration does not stop the release.
